text:
alex: Pushed an nsys trace from a 30s run that mimics our 99th-percentile burst (small prompts + frequent new conversations). link: https://perf.redwood/internal/traces/1799998888.nsys :eyes:
perf-bot: Trace uploaded: https://perf.redwood/internal/traces/1799998888.nsys (size 28MB).
mira: quick summary? what's the top-level time sink?
alex: Short: ~42% of GPU time is in trtExecuteAsync/cublas kernels, but ~18% is in wrapper-level memcpy + setup (host->device memcpy + descriptor builds). Scheduler itself shows ~9% in vllm::Scheduler::dispatch and ~6% in waiting on engine futures.
jon: can you paste the nsys flame snippet?
alex: Sure — pasted below (nsys timeline rows simplified):

```
GPU Timeline (slice):
[wrapper memcpy]  |====|  120us
[scheduler ]      |-|      40us
[engine call]     |==========|  300us  (trtExecuteAsync -> cublasLtMatmul)
[kvcache hit]     |==|     30us
[cuda sync]       |--|     20us
```

Sample counts: kernel launches 8000, memcpy ops 7200, small kernels (pointwise) are ~35% of kernel calls but tiny individually.
mira: Interesting. Wrapper memcpy being that high suggests batching window too small or we are re-uploading tokens each invoke. Are these requests with cold KV cache?
alex: No, workload uses prefix caching but split across 4 KV shards. We see repeated small memcpyHtoDAsync per shard because we currently pin shards per-engine and sometimes move slices between engines.
tess: Could that be due to our KV sharding policy + engine selection mismatch? If scheduler moves a request to a different engine it'll reupload the shard slice.
jon: Also curious about kernel selection: are we switching between int8 and fp16 kernels mid-request? That would cause extra setup.
alex: We logged kernel selection traces — we do fall back from fp8->fp16 for certain sequence length combos. The trace shows ~3% of time in kernel selection code (compilation/desc setup) and another ~2% in reinstantiateEngine path.
mira: Any regressed perf compared to last week baseline?
alex: Compared to baseline (last deployed commit) median latency same, but P99 up ~12ms. The P99 correlates with requests that cross engine boundary (i.e., scheduler moved them).
jon: Hypothesis list: 1) KV shard movement causing memcpy overhead, 2) dynamic kernel selection/engine reinstantiate on rare shapes, 3) batching heuristics causing small batch flushes.
tess: Proposed experiments:
- Run nsys with NVTX ranges per step to isolate: wrapper, scheduler, engine, kvcache. Command I used: 
  nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --output=1799998888_dump --force --sample=none --duration=30 \n  --capture-range=nvtx --nvtx-include="wrapper,scheduler,engine,kvcache" -- ./bench_simulate --workload small-burst
- Run microbench where KV shards are pinned never-to-move to see if memcpy disappears.
- Disable dynamic kernel fallback (env ENGINE_KERNEL_SEL=static_fp16) to measure selection overhead.
alex: I already ran a focused trace with KV pinning — wrapper memcpy dropped by ~60% and overall GPU busy time ↓ by ~9%. So KV movement is a big part.
mira: Good find. Next, can we avoid moving shards by biasing scheduler affinity? Maybe best-effort affinity with background compaction.
jon: I'll try scheduler affinity patch: prefer engine that already has requested shard (fall back after 50ms). I'll run with the same nsys command and compare.
tess: Also let's add a perf counter in the wrapper to aggregate memcpy bytes/sec and count how many distinct shards uploaded per request. That will help quantify.

alex: One oddity: when engine chooses a custom kernel (cublasLtMatmul v2) we see an extra 150us stall before kernel start where runtime does cuEventRecord + cuStreamWaitEvent across streams. Could be our wrapper using different streams causing sync.
mira: If wrapper and engine use different streams we need proper event handoff. Maybe we can reuse engine stream or use stream pool.

jon: Plan and owners:
- jon: prototype scheduler affinity & run nsys (expected today).
- tess: add wrapper counters + small benchmark for shard uploads (today).
- alex: instrument kernel-selection logging and run static_fp16 experiment (tomorrow).
- mira: review stream/event handoff in wrapper + propose stream-pinning change (tomorrow).
alex: Quick note: when you upload traces, mark them with NVTX tags `wr:W`, `sch:S`, `eng:E`, `kv:K` so perf-bot can auto-aggregate.
perf-bot: Acknowledged. New trace will be grouped in the dashboard under "wrapper-kv-affinity".
mira: Anything else? we should also measure CPU overhead: scheduler polling shows small but steady 6% CPU which might amplify tail.
jon: I'll add a perf stat capture for CPU (perf record) in the microbench.
alex: OK let's sync after we have the three traces (baseline, kv-pinned, affinity). I'll post comparisons in this thread and open a tiny PR to gate affinity behind a flag. :thumbsup:
mira: thanks all.
jon: on it.
